title: HF28 (2019-2020 Regular): Firearm transfer criminal background checks required.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/91/2019/0/HF/28/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced text (as filed); no later amendments. Section 1 strikes the transferee permit renewal, the permit-to-carry shortcut, and the one-year term; Section 2 strikes the "transfer to unknown party" identity rule and the "transferee permit" subdivision; those are not quoted. Penalty changes (felony for false statement) are for the bill's own gun rule. Effective August 1, 2019.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 6): (a) A transferee permit issued pursuant to this section is valid statewide for the transfer of a single firearm and shall expire immediately after either: (1) the holder receives a firearm from a transferor, unless the transfer is excluded under section 624.7134, subdivision 6; or (2) 30 days have elapsed from the date the transferee permit was issued to the holder.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 11): A person who makes a false statement in order to obtain a transferee permit knowing or having reason to know the statement is false is guilty of a felony.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 1): Except as provided in this section and section 624.7131, every person who agrees to transfer a firearm shall report the following information in writing to the chief of police of the organized full-time police department of the municipality where the proposed transferee resides or to the appropriate county sheriff if there is no such local chief of police:
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 4): No person shall deliver a firearm to a proposed transferee after receiving a written notification that the chief of police or sheriff has determined that the proposed transferee is prohibited by section 624.713 from possessing a firearm.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): A person who is not a firearms dealer is prohibited from transferring possession or ownership of a firearm to any other person who is not a firearms dealer, unless the transferee presents a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131 and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3): (a) When two parties complete the transfer of a firearm under subdivision 2, the transferor and transferee must complete a record of transfer on a form designed and made publicly available without fee for this purpose by the superintendent of the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. (d) Both the transferor and the transferee must retain a copy of the record of transfer and any attachments to the record of transfer.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 4): (b) A person who refuses or is unable to produce a record of transfer for a firearm transferred under this section in response to a request for production made by a peace officer pursuant to paragraph (a) is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.
Section 3 (Minn.
